items.finding: Whiting et al. (2015) has four JAMA correction notices; a first reader's card gives DOIs 10.1001/jama.2015.8253, 10.1001/jama.2015.9010, 10.1001/jama.2015.15929 and 10.1001/jama.2016.3470, not yet verified; every number of the medical claims to be checked against the corrected values.
items.reason: All four DOIs exist in Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/<DOI>, read in my own tab): 'Incorrect Figure Label', JAMA 2015;314(5):520 (4 Aug 2015); 'Incorrect Values Reported', 314(8):837 (25 Aug 2015); 'Incorrect Nonproprietary Drug Name and Approved Use', 314(21):2308 (1 Dec 2015); 'Incorrect Effect Estimate', 315(14):1522 (12 Apr 2016); they match the four PubMed errata in the reference record. Crossref carries no update-to links, so the link to Whiting et al. rests on the notices themselves, each of which cites the article as its reference 1. Notices read on their JAMA pages (fullarticle/2422523, 2429689, 2473469, 2512765; the second showed a check page on the first attempt, which I did not touch; a plain reload several minutes later loaded it): (1) Figure 4's axis labels swapped, no number changed; (2) the abstract's Ashworth value should read WMD -0.12 (95% CI -0.24 to 0.01), 5 trials, which is the value the claims use (the notice says nothing about Table 2); (3) Table 1's ajulemic acid row: name (JBT-101, CT3), not currently in clinical use (no claim uses it); (4) the 5th sentence of the Sleep Disorder section: nabilone associated with improvements in insomnia (-3.25, -5.26 to -1.24) and greater restfulness (0.48, 0.01 to 0.95), no effect on results, which is the wording and the numbers the claims use. The saved article text carries all four corrections. Every number of the five medical claims was rechecked against the corrected article: none differs.
items.evidence: Crossref works records and the four notice pages, 2026-10-31; notes in scratchpad/can-a/a244/crossref_whiting_corrections.txt; card sc_whiting_2015 replication.timeline updated

for_senior_author: Medical claims rest on one 2015 review (Whiting et al.; AMSTAR 2 critically low, provisional): later reviews on the project's lists (Stockings et al. 2018, Wang et al. 2021, McDonagh et al. 2022 on pain; Black et al. 2019 on mental-health conditions) are unread, and no trial of cannabidiol medicines in epilepsy (for example Devinsky et al. 2017) is on the lists; the other-conditions claim now says so. Decide whether to add them before these claims are shown.

Status 'replicated' for chronic pain and MS spasticity is a close call: in Figure 2, 3 of 8 responder trials point towards placebo (none significantly), and the review calls the continuous results not consistent across trials; per-trial results of the patient-rated spasticity pool are not shown.
